p2_b11.ocr: few dogs in the untreated control groups developed signs of FAD, and then only in two of the six long-term studies. This suggests that other factors may also have been involved in the latter two studies. Since the clinical signs of FAD are directly related to exposure to flea bites, there are two main strategies in treating animals exhibiting this allergic reaction. The first is to reduce the animal’s exposure to flea bites and the second is to administer appropriate palliative treat- ment to reduce the pruritus and inflammation. A com- bination of both strategies usually produces the best results.
